items.headline: Google turns off Search for schools that reject AI tools
items.summary: Google announced it will restrict its Search engine for schools that block its AI tools, while giving schools options to limit the built-in chatbot from doing students' work. The move follows a WSJ investigation and bipartisan Senate inquiry into Google's AI rollout in education.

items.headline: Google brings Guided Learning to Search and Classroom globally
items.summary: Google is launching Guided Learning into Google Classroom worldwide and bringing its capabilities to Search, alongside updated controls for Gemini and student accounts. The updates reshape how AI is deployed across K-12 education.

items.headline: OpenAI claims models disproved exponential time hypothesis
items.summary: OpenAI announced its models disproved the exponential time hypothesis, upending a foundational assumption in computer science, while Anthropic says its models independently reached the same discovery. The claims escalate a wave of AI-driven mathematical breakthroughs after recent Navier-Stokes work.

items.headline: OpenAI employees warned about security lapses for years
items.summary: Sources told Reuters that OpenAI employees raised concerns about operational security lapses over several years. The report raises fresh questions about how the AI leader protects its models and infrastructure.

items.headline: AI stocks sell off as markets eye US midterm elections
items.summary: Asian shares fell and U.S. futures edged lower as technology and AI stocks faced selling pressure amid concerns prices rose too high. Investors watched the U.S. midterm elections, which could constrain AI buildout and fiscal spending.

items.headline: Anthropic updates usage policy on model abuse
items.summary: Anthropic added a prohibition on sustained, needless abusive behavior toward its models, applying only in extreme cases. The update aligns with allowing Claude to end conversations with persistently abusive users.

items.headline: Google recaps October AI updates led by Gemini 4
items.summary: Google published a recap of its biggest October AI updates, highlighting Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon alongside its new Genie 4 world model. The roundup underscores Google's accelerating frontier model cadence.

items.headline: OpenAI plans new security sprint to harden systems
items.summary: OpenAI announced its next internal security sprint, bringing in outside researchers and partners including Cathedral Systems to test its systems using its own models. The effort reflects growing scrutiny of AI lab security.

items.headline: Snowflake unveils autonomous data engineering for AI agents
items.summary: Snowflake announced new autonomous data engineering and real-time analytics innovations, including CoCo Cloud Agents that handle recurring pipeline fixes with engineer guardrails. The tools aim to build the trusted data foundation AI agents rely on.

items.headline: Trump declares war on the term 'artificial intelligence'
items.summary: President Trump wants everyone to replace the term 'artificial intelligence' with 'superintelligence,' putting Silicon Valley leaders in an awkward messaging position. The branding push tests tech CEOs' alignment with the White House.

items.headline: Google expands AI Educator Series to five new countries
items.summary: Google's AI Educator Series is expanding to Spain, Brazil, Mexico, Australia, and sub-Saharan Africa. The program aims to train teachers worldwide on integrating AI into classrooms.

items.headline: Agility Robotics to go public via $465M SPAC deal
items.summary: Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI announced a business combination closing November 4 with roughly $465 million in gross capital, backed by NVIDIA, Amazon, and SoftBank. The combined company will trade on Nasdaq under ticker 'AGLT' starting November 5.

items.headline: AI cited in over 120,000 of 2026's US job cuts
items.summary: Artificial intelligence was cited in 120,136 of the 573,195 U.S. job cuts announced through September, more than any other reason this year, per Challenger, Gray & Christmas. Tech companies led the layoffs with over 165,000 cuts.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO becomes referendum on Big Tech spending
items.summary: Anthropic has committed hundreds of billions in compute to half the Magnificent Seven, making its upcoming IPO a high-stakes test of AI's financial viability. The Claude maker is on the hook to pay Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft tens of billions each.

items.headline: OpenAI releases updated Model Spec for frontier AI
items.summary: OpenAI published an updated Model Spec aimed at making its models more capable and beneficial, alongside new research on detecting frontier model misalignment. The updates reflect evolving safety and alignment practices.

items.headline: Meta unveils Muse Spark Open, top US open-weights model
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, which it bills as the new top U.S. open-weights model, capable of running on two paired Mac desktops. The release intensifies competition in the open-weights model landscape.

items.headline: Microsoft cloud growth accelerates amid soaring AI spend
items.summary: Microsoft's cloud growth accelerated alongside rising capital expenditures, as AI labs like Anthropic commit at least $44.9 billion to Microsoft compute through 2033. The figures highlight how hyperscalers are benefiting from AI labs' compute needs.

items.headline: AI data center measures on ballots in 13 US states
items.summary: Thirteen U.S. states have AI data center-related measures on the ballot, with 84% of 49 measures decided in the November midterms. Candidates in 20 gubernatorial races are calling for moratoriums on AI data centers.
